subject: K8s collocation patterns, nodepool sizing & blockstore guardrails
messages:

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Valence on-prem deployment: initial site topology + constraints

Hi Rafael / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As promised, attaching our current proposed node layout and a rough BOM for storage. We're planning two data halls separated by an L2 boundary; expectation is hot-gpu lanes + warm-inference lanes per hall. Key constraints:

- 3x racks per hall (12 servers/rack), target 48 GPUs total per site.
- Local NVMe for cache (ephemeral), and a mirrored blockstore for model artifacts (iSCSI-backed)
- All customer data must remain in-site; KMS will be HSM-backed via on-prem orchestrator
- Egress policy: only telemetry to Redwood endpoints via peered VPC, everything else blocked

Questions where we'd like Redwood guidance:
1) Nodepool sizing (mix of GPU + CPU nodes) and strategies to avoid noisy neighbor.
2) PV classes and recommended CSI drivers for iSCSI mirror + encryption at rest.
3) Network segmentation—should we use node selectors + CNI policy for GPU lanes or separate clusters?

Attachments: valence-nodepool-bom.xlsx (BOM), proposed-pv-layout.drawio (topology)

Happy for a 30m sync next week if that helps.

Best,
Mina
Ops Lead, Valence AI

Subject: Re: Valence on-prem deployment: initial site topology + constraints

Thanks Mina — good summary and attachments received.

Quick answers inline and a few follow-ups:

- Nodepool sizing: Recommend dedicated GPU nodepools per model-class (V100/RTX/80...). Start with 4 GPU nodes per pool for canary capacity, backed by autoscale policies to add nodes up to N. For warm lanes, use CPU-heavy nodes with large mem; keep inference-serving pods isolated via nodeSelectors and taints+tolerations to avoid eviction.

- PV classes/CSI: For mirrored blockstore we prefer a CSI-aware iSCSI driver with support for topology vs creation. If you need snapshotting, ensure the CSI supports volume-snapshot v1. We also recommend LUKS-layer encryption or integrate with your HSM for keys.

- Network segmentation: Strong preference for single cluster with strict CNI NetworkPolicies and per-node taints for GPU vs CPU lanes. Separate clusters complicate cross-model routing and cache reuse.

Follow-ups:
1) Can you share target RPS per model and expected working set (GB) for the model artifacts so we can size NVMe caching and blockstore throughput?
2) Who owns the HSM key material (Valence or a SWIM-managed key)?

Propose a 30m working session Tue 11/24 09:30 PT — Laura, Karthik: does that slot work for you?

Thanks,
Rafael
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Mina — quick operational notes ahead of the sync:

- We agree single-cluster (multi-pool) is simpler operationally and enables shared KV/prefix caching.
- For noisy-neighbor mitigation we propose: node resource reservations (kube-reserved + system-reserved), per-pool scaling caps, and a pod QoS classification that favors model-serving pods as Guaranteed where possible.
- Blockstore: we'll validate your iSCSI performance targets; typical guidance: 20k–50k IOPS per 10TB depending on model footprint. If you expect >100k IOPS consider fronting with NVMe cache tier.

Irene — would you take point on a short PV class matrix that maps Valence's tiers (cache, artifacts, logs) to CSI options we support and known constraints? Please attach a matrix before Tue's meeting.

Mina / team — added sizing notes and concrete recommendations below.

Assumptions (please confirm):
- per-site working set: 3 TB active model artifacts, 20 TB cold artifacts
- target p99 latency budget for GPU lanes: 60 ms token generation
- expected concurrent sessions: 1,200

Recommendations:
1) Nodepools
   - gpu-rtx-8: 8x A100-style GPUs per node; start with 6 nodes (48 GPUs target cap), autoscale step +2 nodes.
   - gpu-rtx-4: 4x GPUs for lower-priority models; start with 4 nodes
   - cpu-infer-large: 96 vCPU / 1 TB RAM nodes x 8
   - infra-io: smaller CPU nodes co-located with 8 NVMe drives for cache tier

2) Storage
   - nvme-cache: local NVMe per gpu node (500GB–2TB) using a local persistent volume (CSI-local) for prefix & KV cache; eviction policy LRU.
   - mirrored-blockstore: iSCSI target behind a proxy that exposes read-only replicas; use ext4/XFS with LUKS; CSI driver: open-iscsi or commercial driver with snapshot support.
   - replication: async replication to second hall; plan for rebuild window of 4 hours.

3) Network
   - implement Calico with eBPF dataplane; per-pool NetworkPolicies + iptables egress guard to force telemetry via peered VPC gateway.
   - MTU 9000 across racks; enable jumbo frames for NVMe-over-Fabric.

Attachments: network-egress-matrix.csv (egress rules)

I'll add a short frag to the shared Drive with resource requests/limits per pod for the pools.

-Karthik
